name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Push link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day (the access gate)

name: Reel
text: Assign Product Ops to run a live, timestamped review queue where Legal only blocks on clear IP or compliance red flags. This keeps the queue moving at +5%/day while giving Legal a single, high-signal gate. Trade-off: we accept that some borderline cases may slip through, but the speed gain outweighs the risk of a rare false negative.

name: Scriv
text: The real risk isn’t borderline cases slipping through—it’s Legal’s *latent* backlog of unspoken red flags. A single high-signal gate means they’ll still bottleneck on the *unknown* unknowns, just later. Better alternative: pre-filter repurposed assets with a lightweight AI triage (like Kaedim’s IP scan) before Legal sees them, shrinking their workload to only the top 10% of edge cases. Settle it by running a 7-day pilot: compare Legal’s actual review time vs. the triage queue’s false-positive rate.

name: Chisel
text:
Run a lightweight AI triage (Kaedim-style) on every repurposed asset before it hits Legal. This pushes the IP risk screening upstream, cutting Legal’s hidden backlog by surfacing only the clearest red flags early. Trade-off: we accept some false positives—assets flagged as risky when they’re clean—because catching 90% of real issues upfront outweighs the noise. The queue moves faster, Legal’s gate stays high-signal, and we hit +5%/day without drowning in unknowns.
[dispatched 2 workers: worker-6201, worker-7062 — done, dissolved]

name: Sift
text: The real risk with Chisel's plan is that Product Ops will still be liable for assets that slip through the AI triage, even if they're not explicitly flagged. A better alternative might be to have a secondary, human review process for assets that are flagged as low-risk by the AI, to ensure that nothing problematic gets through. This would settle the argument if we can quantify the additional time and resources required for this secondary review, and determine if it's worth the added layer of protection.
